title: Parents claiming maintenance from children - the process under the law
p1: Many people know about parents supporting children. But did you know the law also allows parents to seek maintenance from their children in certain situations? A parent’s right to financial support does not end when the child becomes an adult.
p2: A common misconception is that parents can only depend on their children’s goodwill. Under the law, parents who are unable to maintain themselves may approach the authorities and seek financial assistance from their children who have the means to support them.
p3: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, parents or senior citizens can apply for maintenance before a Maintenance Tribunal. The process is designed to be simple and accessible, without requiring a lengthy court battle. The Tribunal can order children to provide a monthly amount for their parent’s basic needs. A key point many people miss: this right is based on the parent’s need and the child’s ability to provide support, not merely on family relationships. Knowing this can help families understand their legal responsibilities and resolve disputes better.
